nodes.summary: The instruction count $\ell(a)$ of an arithmetic expression $a$ is defined by recursion on $a$: a constant or a variable has count $1$, and if $a$ is the sum, difference or product of $a_1$ and $a_2$, then $\ell(a) = \ell(a_1) + \ell(a_2) + 1$.
nodes.title: Instruction count of an arithmetic expression

nodes.summary: The instruction count $\ell(b)$ of a Boolean expression $b$ is defined by recursion on $b$, using the instruction count $\ell(a)$ of arithmetic expressions $a$: a truth value has count $1$; the tests $a_1 = a_2$ and $a_1 \le a_2$ have count $\ell(a_1) + \ell(a_2) + 1$; the negation of $b_1$ has count $\ell(b_1) + 1$; and the conjunction of $b_1$ and $b_2$ has count $\ell(b_1) + \ell(b_2) + 1$.
nodes.title: Instruction count of a Boolean expression

nodes.summary: The compiled code of an arithmetic expression is the list of stack-machine instructions defined by recursion: a constant $n$ compiles to the single instruction push $n$, a variable $x$ to the single instruction load $x$, and the sum, difference or product of $a_1$ and $a_2$ to the code of $a_1$, then the code of $a_2$, then the single instruction add, sub or mul respectively.

Let $C_0(c)$ be the compiled code of $c$ at base program counter $0$ and $\ell(c)$ the instruction count of $c$. Then the stack machine running $C_0(c)$ goes in finitely many steps from program counter $0$, the empty stack and state $s$ to program counter $\ell(c)$, the empty stack and state $s'$.

nodes.title: Compilation of commands

nodes.summary: A configuration of the stack machine is a triple $(pc, \sigma, s)$ of a program counter $pc \in \mathbb{N}$, a stack $\sigma$, which is a finite list of natural numbers whose head is the top of the stack, and a state $s$ assigning a natural number to each variable.
nodes.title: Stack machine configurations

nodes.summary: For every program $P$, the step relation of the stack machine running $P$ is deterministic: if a configuration $x$ steps to $y$ and to $z$, then $y = z$. The fetched instruction and the shape of the stack determine the next configuration.
nodes.title: Determinism of the stack machine

nodes.summary: Let $B$, $S$ and $A$ be lists of instructions and let $i < |S|$ be a natural number. Then the instruction at position $|B| + i$ of the concatenation $B\,S\,A$ of the three lists equals the instruction at position $i$ of $S$, positions being counted from $0$.
nodes.title: Fetching from an embedded code segment

nodes.summary: An instruction of the stack machine is one of $\mathsf{push}\ n$, $\mathsf{load}\ x$ and $\mathsf{store}\ x$ for natural numbers $n$ and $x$; the arithmetic instructions $\mathsf{add}$, $\mathsf{sub}$ and $\mathsf{mul}$; the comparison and Boolean instructions $\mathsf{eq}$, $\mathsf{le}$, $\mathsf{not}$ and $\mathsf{and}$; and the jumps $\mathsf{jump}\ t$ and $\mathsf{jumpIfZero}\ t$ for a natural number $t$. nodes.title: Stack machine instructions

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a program, that is a list of instructions, and let $(pc, \sigma, s)$ be a configuration with $|P| \le pc$. Then the stack machine running $P$ has no step from $(pc, \sigma, s)$ to any configuration, since there is no instruction at position $pc$ to fetch.
nodes.title: No step past the end of the program

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a program, that is a list of instructions, and write $a :: \sigma$ for the stack with top $a$ above the stack $\sigma$. A configuration $(pc, \sigma, s)$ steps to a configuration $c'$ under $P$ exactly when $pc < |P|$ and, for the instruction at position $pc$ of $P$ (counted from $0$), one of the following holds, where $s[x \mapsto v]$ is the state $s$ with variable $x$ set to $v$.
nodes.title: Step relation of the stack machine

nodes.summary: For a program $P$, the multi-step relation on configurations is the reflexive transitive closure of the step relation of the stack machine running $P$: it relates $c$ to $c'$ when $c'$ is obtained from $c$ by zero or more steps.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
